title: Complete 31 Dynasties of Egypt (Manetho Loeb, Palermo Stone/Breasted, Willockx 1-6, Budge Vol. II) + Complete Ptolemies & Napata/Meroe Kings

nodes.name: Manetho's Pre-Dynastic Rulers: Gods (Ptah→Re→Shu→Geb→Osiris→Seth→Horus), Demigods & Shemsu-Hor ('Spirits of the Dead')
nodes.era: Predynastic Mythic Era (Manetho Fr. 1-4, Loeb pp. 3-19)
nodes.role: 24,900 Lunar Years of Divine & Demigod Kingship Before Menes
nodes.notes: Manetho's opening sequence: 6 Great Gods (Hephaestus/Ptah -> son Helios/Re -> Agathodaemon/Shu -> Cronos/Geb -> Osiris & Isis -> Typhon/Seth), 9 Demigods (Horus, Ares/Anhur, Anubis, Heracles/Khonsu, Apollo, Ammon, Tithoes, Sosus, Zeus), down to Bydis/Bites and the Shemsu-Hor ('Followers of Horus / Spirits of the Dead').

nodes.name: Palermo Stone Predynastic Kings of Lower Egypt (Seka, Khayu, Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazner, Mekh) & King Scorpion
nodes.era: c. 3200-3000 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §90, p. 57)
nodes.role: Earliest Historically Inscribed Rulers of the Nile Before Narmer
nodes.notes: Row 1 of the 5th-Dynasty Palermo Stone preserves actual names of Pre-Unification Red Crown Kings of Lower Egypt: Seka, Khayu, Teyew/Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazenez/Wazner, and Mekh — alongside Upper Egyptian Dynasty 0 rulers Iry-Hor, Ka, and King Scorpion.

nodes.name: Dynasty I Complete (Thinite, 8 Kings): Narmer/Menes → Hor-Aha (Athothis) → Djer (Kenkenes) → Djet (Uenephes) → Queen Merneith → Den (Usaphais) → Adjib (Miebis) → Semerkhet (Semempses) → Qa'a (Bieneches)
nodes.era: c. 2982-2803 BCE (Willockx pp. 7-8; Manetho Fr. 6-7)
nodes.role: Complete Unification Dynasty (Africanus Makes Every King Son of His Predecessor)
nodes.notes: 179 historical years (Manetho: 253 yrs). Queen Merneith ruled as regent/mother of Den. Every Abydos royal tomb and Horus-name matched with Manetho's Greek names.

nodes.name: Dynasty II Complete (9 Kings): Hotepsekhemwy (Boethos) → Nebre (Kaiechos) → Nynetjer (Binothris) → Weneg (Tlas) → Sened (Sethenes) → Sneferka → Sekhemib → Seth-Peribsen (Sesochris) → Khasekhemwy (Cheneres)
nodes.era: c. 2803-2657 BCE (Willockx pp. 9-10; Manetho Fr. 8-10)
nodes.role: Consolidation of Memphis & Horus/Seth Reconciliation
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Nynetjer (Binothris) it was decreed that women could hold the royal dignity; Peribsen took a Seth-name before Khasekhemwy united both Horus and Seth above his serekh!

nodes.name: Dynasty III Complete (Memphite, 5 Kings): Sanakht (Necherophes) → Netjerykhet/Djoser (Tosorthros + Imhotep) → Sekhemkhet (Tyris) → Khaba → Huni (Kerpheres)
nodes.era: c. 2657-2589 BCE (Willockx p. 11; Manetho Fr. 11-12)
nodes.role: Dawn of Stone Pyramid Architecture (Saqqara Step Pyramid)
nodes.notes: Djoser & architect Imhotep (Greek: Imuthes/Asclepius) built the first monumental stone pyramid; Huni inaugurated the royal cartouche.

nodes.name: Dynasty IV Complete (Pyramid Builders, 7 Kings): Sneferu (Soris) → Khufu (Suphis I) → Djedefre (Ratoises) → Khafre (Suphis II) → Baka (Bicheris) → Menkaure (Mencheres) → Shepseskaf (Sebercheres) & Queen Khentkawes
nodes.era: c. 2589-2454 BCE (Willockx p. 12; Manetho Fr. 14-16)
nodes.role: Complete Great Pyramid Dynasty of Dahshur & Giza
nodes.notes: Sneferu built 3 giant pyramids; sons/grandsons Khufu, Djedefre, Khafre, and Menkaure erected Giza; Menkaure's daughter Queen Khentkawes bridged Dynasties IV and V!

nodes.name: Dynasty V Complete (Solar Kings, 9 Kings): Userkaf (Usercheres) → Sahure (Sephres) → Neferirkare Kakai → Shepseskare → Neferefre → Nyuserre Ini → Menkauhor → Djedkare Isesi → Unas (Onnus, Pyramid Texts!)
nodes.era: c. 2454-2297 BCE (Willockx pp. 13-14; Manetho Fr. 18)
nodes.role: Sun Temple Builders & Oldest Religious Texts (Pyramid Texts of Unas)
nodes.notes: Userkaf's era compiled the Palermo Stone Annals; Unas inscribed the oldest corpus of sacred funerary liturgy in human history (Pyramid Texts) inside his Saqqara pyramid.

nodes.name: Dynasty VI Complete (6-7 Kings): Teti (Othoes) → Userkare → Pepi I (Phius) → Merenre I → Pepi II (Phiops, 94-yr reign!) → Merenre II → Queen Nitocris (Neith-iqerty)
nodes.era: c. 2297-2168 BCE (Willockx pp. 15-16; Manetho Fr. 20-21)
nodes.role: Longest Reign in History (Pepi II) & End of the Old Kingdom
nodes.notes: Pepi II ascended at age 6 and ruled into his 90s (Manetho: 94 yrs!). Manetho & Herodotus name Queen Nitocris ('bravest and most beautiful woman of her time') closing the Old Kingdom.

nodes.name: First Intermediate Period (Dynasties VII–X): Memphite Ephemerals (Neferkare Pepyseneb) & Heracleopolitan Kings (Khety / Achthoes I–III, Merikare)
nodes.era: c. 2168-2040 BCE (Manetho Fr. 23-30; Breasted Vol. I)
nodes.role: Fragmented Rival Houses of Memphis & Heracleopolis
nodes.notes: Manetho's famous '70 kings in 70 days' (Dyn. VII) and Khety/Achthoes of Heracleopolis (Dyn. IX-X, author of 'Teaching for King Merikare').

nodes.name: Dynasty XI Complete (Theban Reunifiers): Intef I → Intef II → Mentuhotep I → Intef III → Mentuhotep II (Reunified Egypt!) → Mentuhotep III → Mentuhotep IV
nodes.era: c. 2160-2000 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §63; Manetho Fr. 31-32)
nodes.role: Theban Unifiers of the Middle Kingdom
nodes.notes: Mentuhotep II defeated Heracleopolis, reunited Upper & Lower Egypt, and built the terraced mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari.

nodes.name: Dynasty XII Complete (Golden Age of Middle Kingdom): Amenemhat I → Senusret I (Sesonchosis) → Amenemhat II → Senusret II → Senusret III (Sesostris) → Amenemhat III (Lamares, Labyrinth!) → Amenemhat IV → Queen Sobekneferu (Scemiophris)
nodes.era: 2000-1788 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §64; Manetho Fr. 34-36)
nodes.role: Classical Peak of Egyptian Literature, Faiyum Irrigation & Nubian Fortresses
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves direct parent-child links: Amenemhat I -> son Senusret I -> Amenemhat II -> Senusret II -> Senusret III -> son Amenemhat III (built the Great Labyrinth at Hawara) -> Amenemhat IV -> sister Queen Sobekneferu (first fully attested female Pharaoh!).

nodes.name: Dynasties XIII (60 Theban Kings: Sobekhotep IV / Chenephres, Dedumose / Tutimaeus) & XIV (76 Xoite Kings of the Eastern Delta)
nodes.era: c. 1788-1650 BCE (Manetho Fr. 38-42; Artapanus)
nodes.role: Second Intermediate Period Fragmentation & Asiatic Delta Settlers
nodes.notes: Waddell notes Sobekhotep IV = Chenephres (in Artapanus's Moses account!) and Dedumose = Tutimaeus ('in whose reign a blast of God smote us' and the Hyksos entered Egypt!).

nodes.name: Dynasties XV–XVII: Great Hyksos Kings (Salitis, Bnon, Apachnan, Khyan/Iannas, Apophis/Apepi, Khamudi/Assis) vs. Theban Liberators (Seqenenre Tao & Kamose)
nodes.era: c. 1650-1550 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42-49 via Josephus Against Apion)
nodes.role: Semitic Shepherd Kings of Avaris & War of Liberation
nodes.notes: Josephus (quoting Manetho verbatim!) preserved the 6 Great Hyksos rulers of Avaris (Salitis, Bnon, Apachnan, Apophis [traditional Pharaoh of Joseph in Syncellus!], Khyan, Assis) until Theban Seqenenre Tao & son Kamose launched the liberation finished by Ahmose I.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Early–Mid: Ahmose I → Amenhotep I → Thutmose I → Thutmose II & Queen Hatshepsut (Amessis) → Thutmose III → Amenhotep II → Thutmose IV
nodes.era: 1550-1391 BCE (Manetho Fr. 50-53; Breasted Vol. I)
nodes.role: Imperial Expansion to the Euphrates & Sole Female Pharaoh Hatshepsut
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Hatshepsut (Manetho's Amessis) sent the famous trade expedition to Punt; Thutmose III (Battle of Megiddo) expanded Egypt to its greatest extent; Thutmose IV erected the Dream Stele between the Sphinx's paws.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Late (Amarna & Post-Amarna): Amenhotep III (+ Queen Tiye) → Akhenaten (+ Nefertiti) → Smenkhkare → Tutankhamun → Ay → Horemheb (Harmais = Danaus!)
nodes.era: 1391-1292 BCE (Manetho Fr. 50-53; Amarna Letters)
nodes.role: Monotheistic Amarna Revolution & Greco-Egyptian Danaus/Aegyptus Bridge
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho explicitly equates General/Pharaoh Horemheb ('Harmais') with Greek Danaus and Ramesses/Seti with his brother Aegyptus — linking Greek Argive genealogy directly into Egypt's 18th/19th Dynasty transition!

nodes.name: Dynasty XIX Complete: Ramesses I → Seti I (Sethos) → Ramesses II (Rapsaces, 67 yrs) → Merneptah (Israel Stele) → Amenmesse → Seti II & Siptah → Queen Twosret (Thuoris — Fall of Troy!)
nodes.era: 1292-1189 BCE (Manetho Fr. 55-56; Breasted Vol. I)
nodes.role: Ramesside Empire & Manetho's Synchronism with the Trojan War
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Queen Twosret ('Thuoris', identified with Homer's Polybus & Alcandra) Troy was taken — synchronizing Egypt's 19th Dynasty directly with the Bronze Age Collapse & Trojan War!

nodes.name: Dynasty XX Complete (10 Ramessides): Setnakhte → Ramesses III (Medinet Habu, Sea Peoples!) → Ramesses IV → V → VI → VII → VIII → IX → X → Ramesses XI
nodes.era: 1189-1077 BCE (Budge Book of Kings Vol. II pp. 1-20; Manetho Fr. 57)
nodes.role: Defense Against the Sea Peoples & End of the New Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Budge Vol. II lists all 10 sons of Ramesses III from Medinet Habu (incl. Ramesses IV, VI, VIII) and the complete Ramesside succession down to Ramesses XI, when High Priest Herihor seized Upper Egypt.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXI (Divided Egypt): Tanite Kings (Smendes, Psusennes I [Silver Pharaoh!], Amenemope, Osochor, Siamun, Psusennes II) & Theban Priest-Kings (Herihor → Piankh → Pinudjem I → Menkheperre → Pinudjem II)
nodes.era: 1077-943 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 20-34; Manetho Fr. 58-59)
nodes.role: Biblical Era of David & Solomon (Siamun & Psusennes II)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Psusennes I's intact silver sarcophagus was found at Tanis; Siamun campaigned in Philistia/Gezer (often identified as the Pharaoh whose daughter married King Solomon, 1 Kgs 3:1, 9:16!); Psusennes II's daughters Karamat & Maatkare married into the Libyan 22nd Dynasty!

nodes.name: Dynasty XXII Complete (Libyan/Bubastite — Stele of Pasenhor): Buiu-uaua → Shoshenq I (Shishak!) → Osorkon I → Takelot I → Osorkon II → Shoshenq II → Takelot II → Shoshenq III → Pami → Shoshenq V
nodes.era: 943-716 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 35-60; Manetho Fr. 60-61)
nodes.role: Complete 15-Generation Meshwesh Libyan Genealogy & Shishak's Sack of Jerusalem
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: The famous Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor (Budge pp. 35-39) traces Shoshenq I back 6 generations to Libyan chief Buyuwawa and forward through Osorkon II! Shoshenq I (= Biblical Shishak, 1 Kgs 14:25) invaded Rehoboam's Judah in 925 BCE.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXIII (Pedubast I, Osorkon III, Takelot III, Rudamun) & XXIV (Tefnakht I → Bakenranef / Bocchoris)
nodes.era: 818-715 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 60-69; Manetho Fr. 62-65)
nodes.role: Libyan Delta Coalitions Resisting Kushite Reunification
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Tefnakht of Sais led the Delta coalition against Kushite King Piye (Piankhi Stele); his son Bakenranef (Greek: Bocchoris, famous lawgiver) was defeated by Kushite Shabaka.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXV Complete (Kushite Pharaohs): Kashta (+ Pebatjma) → Piye & Shabaka (Sabacon) → Shabataka (Sebichos) → Taharqa (Tirhakah) → Tantamani (Ammeris)
nodes.era: 744-656 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 70-78, 195-199; Manetho Fr. 66-67)
nodes.role: Nubian Reunifiers of Egypt & Biblical Allies of Hezekiah
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Budge details the entire royal family including God's Wives of Amun Amenirdis I & Shepenupet II, linking Kushite bloodlines into Dynasty XXVI!

nodes.name: Dynasty XXVI Complete (Saite Renaissance): Necho I → Psamtik I (54 yrs) → Necho II (Battle of Megiddo/Carchemish!) → Psamtik II → Apries (Biblical Hophra!) → Amasis II (44 yrs) → Psamtik III
nodes.era: 664-525 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 78-90; Manetho Fr. 68-69; Jer 44:30)
nodes.role: Last Great Native Renaissance Before Persian Conquest
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Necho II slew King Josiah at Megiddo (609 BCE); Apries (Biblical Pharaoh Hophra, Jer 44:30) sheltered Judean refugees including Jeremiah; Amasis II allied with Croesus of Lydia & Polycrates of Samos; Psamtik III fell to Cambyses II (525 BCE).

nodes.name: Dynasties XXVII–XXXI: 1st Persian (Cambyses, Darius I, Xerxes, Artaxerxes I), XXVIII (Amyrtaeus), XXIX (Nepherites I, Hakor/Achoris), XXX (Nectanebo I, Teos, Nectanebo II — Last Native Pharaoh!) & XXXI (Artaxerxes III, Arses, Darius III)
nodes.era: 525-332 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 91-106; Manetho Fr. 70-75)
nodes.role: Final Native Egyptian Resistance Through Nectanebo II to Alexander (332 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Amyrtaeus freed Egypt from Persia (404 BCE); Nectanebo I & II (Dynasty XXX, builders of Philae & Karnak pylons) were the LAST native Egyptian Pharaohs in history before Alexander the Great entered Egypt in 332 BCE!

nodes.name: Complete Ptolemaic Dynasty (All 15 Ptolemies & 7 Cleopatras): Ptolemy I Soter → II Philadelphus (Septuagint!) → III Euergetes → IV Philopator → V Epiphanes (Rosetta Stone! + Cleopatra I Syra) → VI Philometor → VIII Euergetes II → IX Soter II → XII Auletes → Cleopatra VII & Caesarion
nodes.era: 305-30 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 107-154)
nodes.role: Macedonian-Greek Pharaohs of Alexandria (Septuagint & Rosetta Stone)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ptolemy II built the Library of Alexandria & commissioned the Greek Septuagint; Ptolemy V (+ Seleucid Cleopatra I Syra) issued the Rosetta Stone (196 BCE); Cleopatra VII & Caesarion (Ptolemy XV) closed 3,000 years of Pharaonic rule.

nodes.name: Napatan Kings of Kush: Atlanersa → Senkamanisken → Anlamani → Aspelta → Harsiotef → Nastasen
nodes.era: c. 653-315 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 199-205)
nodes.role: Post-25th Dynasty Nubian Pyramid Builders of Nuri & Jebel Barkal
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 199-205)
nodes.notes: After Assyria pushed Dynasty XXV south of Aswan, Taharqa & Tantamani's successors (Atlanersa, Senkamanisken, Aspelta [moved capital to Meroe after Psamtik II's 593 BCE raid], Harsiotef, Nastasen) ruled Kush for centuries.

nodes.name: Meroitic Kingdom: King Arqamani (Ergamenes) → King Natakamani & Queen Amanitore → Princes Arikhankharer & Shorkaror
nodes.era: c. 270 BCE – 50 CE (Budge Vol. II pp. 205-214; Diodorus III.6; Acts 8:27)
nodes.role: Golden Age of Meroe, Meroitic Script & Biblical Candace Dynasty
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 205-214)
nodes.notes: Arqamani (Greek: Ergamenes, friend of Ptolemy II & IV!) broke priestly control and built Dakka temple; King Natakamani & Kandake Queen Amanitore (Biblical 'Candace' era!) built the Lion Temple at Naqa and restored Meroe.
